Lemma
[existence of rays and lines]

Source: petersen:page-0313, petersen:page-0314 ↗ def:pet-ch7-ray-line ↗ def:pet-ch7-connected-infinity 1. ch7:7.3.1If $p\in (M,g)$ then a ray emanating from $p$ always exists. If $M$ is disconnected at infinity, $(M,g)$ contains a line.
Proof

↗ lem:pet-ch7-ray-line-existence \sketch A ray from $p$ is obtained by taking a limit of minimizing segments to points escaping to infinity. If the manifold is disconnected at infinity, choose segments between escaping points that cross a fixed compact set; after recentering at the crossing points, a subsequential limit is a line.

□
